speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You presented with a two-day history of fever and altered mental status. To understand the severity and cause, can you describe exactly what changes you have noticed in your awareness, such as confusion, delirium, or difficulty staying awake?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning given your age and lack of focal neurological complaints like headache or seizures. Given your history of tics and current use of haloperidol, could you tell me exactly when you started taking this medication and if you have noticed any recent changes in its dosage?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS).

The combination of fever, altered mentation, generalized rigidity, and profuse sweating in a patient currently taking haloperidol is highly characteristic of NMS. Given the severity of these symptoms, immediate discontinuation of the offending agent and supportive care are required.
